The Morning Steep schedule 07:15 AM

Master Brew

The High 'Chhaneko' Pour

Hand-beaten brass kettle, steaming cascade into porous unglazed earthen cups. Frothy, seasoned with freshly cracked ginger root, green cardamom, and fragrant black pepper from eastern hills.

photo_camera Shot by Subash S. • Tokha Main Bar
Terrace Vista

Atmosphere

Morning Mist on Baniyatar Terrace

Reclaimed pine timber benches, slow rising steam against hillside views of northern Kathmandu's emerald ridges. Quiet conversation before the city wakes.

location_on Baniyatar Viewdeck
Local Heritage

Traditional Bites

Crisp Tokha Khaja Platter

Crisp beaten rice (chiura), wood-roasted bhatmas, and spicy timur potato achar served on heavy cast brass thalis. The savory crunch that anchors long afternoon debates.

restaurant Kitchen Batch #4
Hand-Thrown Clay

Bhaktapur Heritage

Earthy Kulhad Artistry

Every cup is thrown on kick-wheels by multi-generational Prajapati potter families in Bolachhen, Bhaktapur. Sun-dried and kiln-baked without synthetic chemical glazes.

palette Prajapati Craft Studio
Adda Culture

Human Warmth

Spirited Evening Guff-Gaff

College debaters, Tokha neighborhood elders, and visiting poets huddled closely around the corner hearth. Where every conversation begins with "चिया कडा बनाइदिनुस न!"

groups 7:30 PM Adda Circle
Hearth Steamer

House Special

Wood-Fired Steamed Momos

Thinly hand-pleated dumplings filled with mountain herbs and spring aromatics, served boiling hot alongside freshly pounded sesame, charred tomato, and roasted garlic chutney.

soup_kitchen Steamer Station #1
Quiet Solitude

Writer's Nook

Quiet Corner with a Book

Natural valley sunlight streaming through timber lattices onto worn pages of Laxmi Prasad Devkota poetry. A haven for slow readers and contemplative afternoons.

menu_book North Reading Window
Daily Genesis

The First Kettle

First Simmer at 6:00 AM

Fresh unpasteurized dairy sourced directly from Tokha valley cowherds, slowly reduced with hand-pounded cinnamon sticks and green Ilam tea leaves in heavy-bottomed brass cauldrons.

flare Early Hearth Batch
Monsoon Magic

Seasonal Romance

Rainy Monsoon Afternoons

Warm shelter, the hypnotic patter of rain drumming on terracotta tiles, fresh fennel malpuwa sizzling in iron skillets, and double-ginger tea with wild mountain honey.
